Perform, perform the sovereignty of the tongue for this self, its function of grasping tastes! Oṃ hāṃ! Perform, perform the sovereignty of the nose for this self, its function of grasping odors! Oṃ hāṃ!
Oṃ hāṃ! Grant to this self the lordship of speech; release speech, *kuru kuru*. Oṃ hāṃ! Grant to this self the lordship of the hands; the capacity to grasp objects, *kuru kuru*. Oṃ hāṃ!
Grant to this self the lordship of the feet; the power of movement, *kuru kuru*. Grant to this self the lordship of the anus...
Perform the function of emission, perform it! Perform the presiding lordship over the generative organ, manifesting bliss, perform it, perform it!
Then, sound and the other objects of the senses, along with their presiding deities, should be installed. Now, the ten channels:
Iḍā, Piṅgalā, and Suṣumnā as the third.
Gāndhārī, Hastijihvā, and Pūṣan are likewise situated there.
"Alampuṣā, Kuhū, and Śāṅkhinī—these are the ten channels (nāḍīs).
Now— prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna;
as well as nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta, and dhanañjaya.
Thus [it is said].
From that, it is clear.
Now, regarding the statement: "In the temple, provided with the five, eight, and eight [units] of earth, water, fire, air, and ether"—
There are the five groups of eight Rudras, as well as the extremely secret group of eight;
then the secret group of eight and the pure group of eight.
Therein, first, in the water-tattva, are the Praṇava, the moon-adorned one (Śiva),
the God of gods, the Unborn (Aja), fragrance, Āṣāḍhā, and that which is named lead (sīsa).
The seventh is Haribhūta, and the eighth is Lakulīśvara;
beyond that comes Agni, and there likewise is Guhyaka.
Hara, Tripuraghna, Triśūla, Sūkṣma,
Mahākāla, Sarva, as well as Īśāna and Bhairava.
Alternatively, the Rudras are situated in the wind; among them, first is Kāmarūpavat,
then Pitāmaha, Vidusthāṇu, and Svayambhūrudra.
Viśva, Mahānāda, and likewise Mahābhīma as the eighth;
Bhava in the sky, Mahā, Trimūrti, and Rudra.
Mahābalaśiva, Sahasrākṣa, Śiva, Kapardin,
Ūrdhvaretas, and Mahotsava reside in the principle of Speech (vāktattva).
Śrīkaṇṭha, Nīlakaṇṭha, and likewise Mahātejas,
as well as Mahāliṅga and Sthūla— thus fifteen are remembered.
Now, those associated with the three qualities (guṇas) are Akṛta, Kṛta, Bhairava, Brāhma, Vaiṣṇava,
Kaumāra, Auma, and Śrīkaṇṭha.
Now, regarding Māyā: Guhaneśa, Aśāṭhya, both Hari and Hara,
Daśeśāna, Mahāvīrya, Trikāla, and likewise Gopati.
Then, at the conclusion of the dissolution, they remained in that same manner above;
[there stood] Lakṣmīśa, the slayer of Brahmā, and beyond him, Vidyeśāna.
Vidyeśa, Śiva, and Ananta are proclaimed as the six Rudras; beyond that,
it is easily understood.
Now, regarding the consecration of a well (*kūpapratiṣṭhā*), one should likewise worship the *vāstu* deity in the circle of the image (*bimba*) when it is divided by twelve,
according to the procedure for the circular mandala of the image; and when divided into nine parts by the number twelve,
the lords of the half-islands are located in the corners of fire, the rakṣas, wind, and the lord of the quarters (the northeast).
From Rudra to the eighth Marut, then in the middle between the corners of Āgneya and Iśāna,

and on the three sides of the center, with the portions mixed together in their respective parts, Parjanya and the others, six-faced ones, are to be worshipped. Furthermore, in the directions starting from the northeast (Īśāna), Āpa and the others are considered to occupy one square each.
The rest is easily understood.
Herein, whatever has not been stated that is complete yet contradicts the established doctrine (siddhānta), and which ought to be corrected with effort by the teachers, is agreed upon [as follows].
The illustrious Kolakī, known as Śaivajanākarākhya, was a king of the Cedis who possessed pure being and was devoted to Śiva;
born of that lineage, he was a knower of the goals of the scriptures of the Śiva doctrine.
Thus says Śrī Dharmaśambhu, the lord of the Gauḍapatis, Nātha.
Therefore,
this teacher Śaṅkara is an ocean of divine scriptures and a wish-fulfilling tree.
Even the inhabitants of heaven obtain his station through mere words,
for they have cast off the singular fear of birth and death.
Then, for the welfare of the world during the Kali age, Śiva indeed became known as Śrī Somaśambhu, pervading the sky of the lineage of Śrī Kolakīya.
Therefore, Jñānaśambhu Sadāśiva has a body composed of the power of knowledge;
by him, everything has been illuminated with the radiant flame of Śiva’s purity.
May he whose feet are honored by the crowns of kings of the lunar and solar dynasties,

who is the sun to the lotus-faces of learned men, and who is the source of compassion for the wretched, the blind, the poets, the miserable, and all beings born on any day or under any constellation— may he protect me.
May the illustrious Jñānaśambhu purify that which is perpetually defiled.

By the power of beholding whom, one indeed attains the state of Śiva after a very long time wandering through the worlds of Lord Lokeśa like a rope; may he, who desires to purify the worlds from the dense impurities of worldly existence, grant us joy.
...rejoicing, [he] whose name is Malabodhaśiva.

The treasure-store of the arrival and departure of the illustrious *Pañcāgama*, possessing a multitude of jewel-like mantras, abiding in the ocean of the six systems of logic, the Smṛtis, and the Vedas, and encircled by the mountain of the true junctures (*sandhi*).

May that Śrī Jñānaśambhu, who incessantly purifies living beings through the eightfold causes of the *vicikā* [initiation], grant me [grace] every day by means of the supreme gift of a Śaiva preceptor.

He who extracts the essence of the flowers of the Siddhānta and Āgama scriptures like a bee, whose voice resounds like a swan, and who has emerged from the lofty tips of the lotus-feet of the venerable one named Jñānaśiva; he who is intent upon the honey-thicket of the lotus-feet of Śrī Someśa.
The illustrious sage Rudradeva, an expert in the Pañcarātra, spoke this which bestows unmanifested awakening;
he is renowned in the world for his asceticism, and this [work] was composed by me concerning him.
Thus [ends the citation].

Thus, in the *Śrīmatsomaśambhupaddhati* composed by the venerable Somaśambhu, or rather in the *Sphuṭabodhinī* commentary composed by Tryambakaśambhu, the fourteenth [section] of the commentary is completed.
Hari Om. May there be auspiciousness.
